name: Kisspeptin

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Hormone family that drives GnRH release

track.title: Pilot in people
track.line: Small hormone and brain-scan studies, 2015 to 2026

track.title: Phase III
track.line: No treatment trial; small physiology studies only

what.text: Kisspeptins are a family of natural peptide hormones. The 2 forms most studied in people are kisspeptin-54 and kisspeptin-10, a short 10-amino-acid piece. Both act on the hypothalamus to release GnRH, the hormone that drives the reproductive system.

src.label: Jayasena et al., Hum Reprod

what.text: How it acts, according to human studies:

items.text: Kisspeptin triggers GnRH release, which makes the pituitary release LH and FSH. In healthy men, kisspeptin-10 and kisspeptin-54 given into a vein raised LH and FSH, but less than GnRH itself.

src.label: Jayasena et al., Hum Reprod

items.text: Given under the skin, kisspeptin-10 raised LH, FSH and testosterone in healthy men. When it was given non-stop for 5 days, LH and FSH fell back to the same levels as with placebo; daily 8-h infusions kept them raised for 12 days.

src.label: Yeung et al., Eur J Endocrinol

items.text: In brain-scan studies, kisspeptin changed activity in brain areas that process sexual and emotional cues.

src.label: Comninos et al., J Clin Invest
Mills et al., JAMA Netw Open

what.text: Kisspeptin is not approved as a medicine anywhere checked. FDA placed kisspeptin-10 in Category 2 in 2023 because of possible safety risks in compounding.

research.text: Human studies of kisspeptin are small physiology studies, many from Imperial College London, plus early-phase trials in the US. They measured hormone release and brain responses over minutes to 12 days. None is a large treatment trial.

research.title: Kisspeptin-10 vs kisspeptin-54 vs GnRH in healthy men (Jayasena et al.)

facts.v: single-blind, placebo-controlled physiology study
healthy men, 5 per dose group
3-h infusions into a vein of vehicle, kisspeptin-10, kisspeptin-54 or GnRH, at 3 doses, on separate days
LH and FSH

research.found: Both kisspeptins raised LH and FSH to a similar degree. GnRH raised LH and FSH about 3 times more than kisspeptin-10 and 2 times more than kisspeptin-54. The authors noted the small sample.

src.label: Jayasena et al., Hum Reprod

research.title: Kisspeptin and sexual and emotional brain processing (Comninos et al.)

facts.v: comparison of kisspeptin vs vehicle, with functional MRI, hormone and questionnaire measures
29 healthy young heterosexual men
single study visits
brain activity in response to sexual and couple-bonding images; mood

research.found: Kisspeptin increased activity in limbic brain areas in response to sexual and bonding images. These changes correlated with measures of reward, drive, mood and sexual aversion, and kisspeptin reduced negative mood.

src.label: Comninos et al., J Clin Invest

research.title: Kisspeptin in men with low sexual desire (Mills et al.)

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-way crossover, single center (ISRCTN17271094)
37 men with hypoactive sexual desire disorder; 32 completed
kisspeptin-54 infused into a vein for 75 minutes, or placebo, at 2 visits at least 7 days apart
brain activity while viewing sexual videos (fMRI), penile tumescence, desire and arousal questionnaires

research.found: Kisspeptin changed activity in the brain’s sexual-processing network compared with placebo. Penile tumescence rose by up to 56% more than placebo, and “happiness about sex” scores rose. Each man got a single infusion; no longer-term effects were tested.

src.label: Mills et al., JAMA Netw Open

research.title: Kisspeptin in women with low sexual desire (Thurston et al.)

facts.v: double-masked, placebo-controlled, 2-way crossover
40 premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder; 32 completed
kisspeptin-54 infused into a vein for 75 minutes, or placebo
brain activity in response to erotic videos and faces

research.found: Kisspeptin changed activity in brain areas for sexual and facial attraction processing. Some changes correlated with sexual distress and aversion scores. No side effects were reported.

src.label: Thurston et al., JAMA Netw Open

research.title: 12 days of kisspeptin-10 under the skin in healthy men (Yeung et al.)

facts.v: randomized, single-blinded, placebo-controlled, 3 sub-studies
15 healthy men given kisspeptin-10, 12 men as controls
infusions of kisspeptin-10 under the skin: 8-h dose-response tests, 5 days non-stop, or 8 h a day for 12 days
up to 12 days
LH, FSH, testosterone

research.found: Kisspeptin-10 raised LH, FSH and testosterone in a dose-dependent way. With non-stop infusion for 5 days, testosterone stayed up but LH and FSH returned to placebo levels. Daily 8-h infusions kept gonadotropins raised for 12 days.

src.label: Yeung et al., Eur J Endocrinol

research.text: Several US trials are sponsored by Stephanie Seminara, MD (earlier ones list Massachusetts General Hospital as sponsor) and use a peptide called kisspeptin 112-121. A phase 2 trial of 2 weeks of pulsatile kisspeptin under the skin in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism is recruiting (NCT05896293, about 36 people). An earlier phase 2 trial in 18 people finished in August 2025 (NCT04648969); no results were found posted. A phase 1 study started in March 2026 (NCT07224490).

us.text: Kisspeptin is not FDA approved for any use. In September 2023 FDA placed kisspeptin-10 in Category 2 for 503A compounding, meaning it raises significant safety risks. It is being tested in phase 1 and 2 trials. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. FDA’s Drugs@FDA data returns no kisspeptin product.

items.text: FDA’s list of bulk substances that may present significant safety risks includes kisspeptin-10 (503A), added September 29, 2023. FDA says compounded kisspeptin-10 may pose a risk of immune reactions for some routes, may have problems with peptide impurities and characterization of the active ingredient, and that FDA has no or only limited safety information for the proposed routes.

world.lead: Kisspeptin is not an authorised medicine in any country checked. It is being studied in research trials. FDA lists kisspeptin-10 as a compounding safety risk. It is banned in sport for men at all times.

countries.status: Not approved. Kisspeptin-10 is in FDA’s 503A Category 2 (significant safety risks) since September 2023. Research use in phase 1 and 2 trials.

after.text: Kisspeptin and its agonist analogues are named under S2.2.1, testosterone-stimulating peptides in males, on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. S2 is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) and its substances are non-Specified. The entry is limited to males. The 2027 list keeps it, in force January 1, 2027.

side.text: Side-effect data are limited to single doses or a few days in small studies. FDA’s concerns for compounded kisspeptin-10 are immune reactions, impurities and a lack of safety data. Long-term effects on hormones and fertility have not been studied.

items.text: FDA says compounded kisspeptin-10 may cause immune reactions for some routes and has complexities with peptide impurities; FDA lacks enough information to know whether it would cause harm in humans.
